newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Singapore, Manchester voted best world airports.
newsitem.headline: Singapore, Manchester voted best world airports.

text.p: Singapore's Changi and Britain's Manchester have been voted the world's top two airports by long distance airline passengers, the International Air Transport Association (IATA) said Wednesday.
Changi's terminal knocked Manchester from the top spot it held last year in the poll of some 55,000 people which rates 54 airports, IATA said.
Passengers were asked to rate from one to 10 the airports where they boarded and left their main long-distance flight on a total of 23 service elements.
Changi, a major transit hub for flights from Europe to Asia and Australasia, was in second place in the 1996 survey.

The top two were closely challenged by Melbourne, Australia, which surged from seventh to third place, Amsterdam, Netherlands, which slipped from third to fourth, and by Zurich, Switzerland, in fifth.
Zurich, increasingly a major centre for traffic into the old Soviet Union and beyond, made the list for the first time.
The Swiss financial center's Kloten airport was voted second best after Changi among business passengers, although it emerged as only ninth among leisure travelers.
Melbourne was rated best in eating facilities with Sydney, Australia, in second place.
Best overall performing U.S. airport was Cincinatti, rated sixth in the poll for passenger convenience because of friendliness of airport staff, restaurant facilities and efficiency of check-in.
Close behind in seventh place was Florida's Orlando, whose staff were rated best for both check-in courtesy and efficiency, followed by Montreal's Mirabel airport, Sydney, and Calgary, Alberta.
